open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the uniform legal inner-neighborhood comparison at possibly vanishing envelope scale, or supply a generic counterexample to it.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen legal-tangent result proves only that derivatives of legal paths lie in the displayed tangent-score domain; it does not prove that the capacity-face directions needed to dominate an empirical increment can be lifted to nearby legal observed laws. The algebraic derivative is explicitly only calibration scaffolding off that domain. In addition, the available multinomial Gaussian approximation is additive, whereas coverage when the conditional envelope quantile tends to zero requires a remainder and critical-value comparison relative to that same shrinking scale. Semialgebraicity and finite face enumeration do not supply either missing inequality, and the legal-realization handle is a construction plan rather than a proved result.
open_obligations.attempted: I extended the prior reduction through the exact conditional-quantile ordering and observed that the full-plane fallback cannot itself cause noncoverage. I also checked the proposed finite-face route: it closes ordinary nondegenerate subsequences, but at empty cells the derivative is rational in the direction and can jump across faces, so an absolute coupling remainder cannot be divided by the vanishing envelope scale. The reported two-cell and Poisson calculations are individual arrays, not a uniform legal-lift certificate or a generic counterexample.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Put
\[
A_n=\left\{\lVert\widehat p_n-p_n\rVert_\infty\le a_n/2\right\},
\qquad r_n=a_n/2.
\]
For each atom coordinate, Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound give
\[
\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M}P_n(A_n^c)
\le 2\lvert\mathcal J\rvert\exp\{-n a_n^2/2\}=o(1),
\]
where the last equality uses \(\sqrt n a_n\to\infty\).  On \(A_n\), every
\(b\in\mathcal B(p_n,r_n)\) satisfies
\[
\lVert b-\widehat p_n\rVert_\infty
\le \lVert b-p_n\rVert_\infty+
\lVert p_n-\widehat p_n\rVert_\infty
\le a_n,
\]
and is legal by the definition of \(\mathcal B(p_n,r_n)\).  Hence
\(\mathcal B(p_n,r_n)\subseteq B_n\), so, for every
\(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal J}\),
\[
T_n(g)\ge E_{p_n,r_n}(g).
\]
Monotonicity of lower quantiles under almost-sure order therefore yields, conditionally on
\(\widehat p_n\),
\[
c_n\ge
Q_{1-\alpha}\!\left\{E_{p_n,r_n}(G^*)\mid\widehat p_n\right\}
\quad\text{on }A_n.
\]
Moreover, either fallback branch makes \(C_n=\mathbb R^2\), so neither
\(B_n=\varnothing\) nor \(M(\widehat p_n)=0\) can cause noncoverage.  Thus the
claimed theorem would follow from the unresolved uniform comparison for the event on which
\(B_n\ne\varnothing\) and \(M(\widehat p_n)>0\), plus the displayed
\(o(1)\) bound.  The frozen core supplies no valid derivation of that comparison in the
vanishing-envelope regime.
